summary:
OrbitQuest is an interactive educational web experience designed to make space exploration more accessible and engaging for students. It transforms the traditional way of learning about the Solar System into an immersive journey through an interactive 3D environment. Users can navigate between planets, rotate and zoom in on the Solar System, adjust orbital motion, and explore selected NASA missions, including Perseverance, Juno, and Cassini.

The project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by providing a visual platform through which students can explore planetary destinations, discover NASA missions, and develop a deeper understanding of space exploration and the technology behind it. By combining interactive visualization with educational content, OrbitQuest aims to turn complex space-related information into an intuitive learning experience. Its modular design also allows future expansion to include more mission histories, scientific instruments, and stories of equipment left behind.
details:
OrbitQuest is a browser-based interactive Solar System explorer. It allows users to experience space through a three-dimensional representation of the planets and their orbital movements.

Users can:

- Explore the Solar System through an interactive 3D model.

- Select individual planets and navigate toward them.

- Rotate the scene by dragging and zoom in or out.

- Control the simulation by adjusting its speed, pausing the animation, and displaying or hiding orbital paths.

- Access selected NASA missions through dedicated mission entry points.

- Explore the relationship between planetary destinations and human-made space exploration technologies.

The experience is designed to encourage active discovery rather than passive reading.

How Does It Work?

The platform combines a 3D visualization environment with interactive navigation controls and educational information.

The Solar System acts as the main interface. Instead of navigating through a conventional list of pages, users interact directly with the celestial environment. Selecting a planet allows the experience to focus on that destination, while the navigation controls make it possible to explore the model from different perspectives.

The mission section provides access to selected NASA missions, connecting the visual experience with real space exploration activities.

Benefits and Expected Impact

OrbitQuest offers several educational benefits:

- Improved understanding: Three-dimensional visualization helps students understand the arrangement and movement of celestial bodies.

- Accessible learning: The web-based format makes the experience available through a standard browser.

- Active engagement: Interactive controls encourage users to explore independently and learn through experimentation.

- Increased scientific curiosity: Connecting planets with NASA missions introduces students to real-world space exploration.

- Educational potential: The platform can be expanded into a learning resource for schools, science clubs, and young astronomy enthusiasts.

Its broader impact is to make scientific knowledge more approachable and encourage students to explore STEM fields, particularly astronomy, physics, and space engineering.
